hyps.why: With edge 5 removed, node 2 does not reach the output, so a conv on edge 1 has no effect instead of its usual gain.
Node 2 is a dead end when edge 5 is none, nullifying the benefit of a conv on edge 2.
If edge 0 is none, node 1 carries zeros, so a conv on edge 1->2 processes nothing.
Edge 4 reads from node 1, which is empty when edge 0 is none, so the conv adds nothing.
The edit is a no-op when edge 5 is already conv3x3, whereas replacing weaker ops usually raises accuracy.
Replacing a conv3x3 on the main path with pooling loses much more accuracy than swapping weaker ops for pooling.
With edge 5 absent, removing edge 3 leaves at most one route into the output, risking a disconnected or very shallow network.
Without the direct 0->3 edge, deleting edge 5 removes a key remaining path to the output, causing a large accuracy drop.
Converting an absent edge into a conv adds a new live path to the output, a larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
With edge 4 removed, node 1 only reaches the output indirectly via edges 2 and 5, reducing the benefit of a conv on edge 0.
